newsitem.title: UK: Russia Vnesh debt falls on Lebed sacking.
newsitem.headline: Russia Vnesh debt falls on Lebed sacking.

text.p: Russian Vneshekonomobank dollar debt dropped on news of the sacking of Russian security chief Alexander Lebed.
Vnesh was quoted at 74 1/2 percent of face value, down from mid-morning highs of around 76 but still above the day's opening low of 74.
However traders said that after the initial reaction there was some support.
"My initial reaction is that probably this will clear the air, and hopefully this will be more positive than the arguing," said John Bunner, at Moscow Narodny Bank in London.
The sacking comes after increasingly public Kremlin infighting, with Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov accusing Lebed of plotting a gradual coup while President Boris Yeltsin awaits heart surgery.
One trader said there was a danger Lebed could now "ditch the dirt", and the market may be in for an unsteady period.
ING Barings chief East Europe economist, Philip Poole, said in the short-term the sacking was positive by removing a source of tension.
"In this very difficult period, the friction he was causing was clearly problematic," he said.
But Poole said the charges against Lebed were implausible and questioned why the ex-general, with such popular appeal, would choose to go outside the constitution to grab power.
It was, however, in Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's interest to undermine Lebed's image.
If Yeltsin were to die in office, Chernomyrdin would take charge of the country until fresh presidential elections could be held. Lebed has been seen as the prime minister's chief rival.
However, it is far from clear how the sacking will affect Lebed's future standing and he could become a focus for the opposition, unrestrained by allegiance to the administration.
"If the mud does not stick, he may come out of it even stronger," Poole added.
